description:
## Goal

Write `test/filament/examples/cart_test.exs` — tests for the Cart example from G2.

Four test groups demonstrating all rungs:
1. **Rung 1** — `Cart.State` pure domain tests (no processes)
2. **Rung 2** — `CartBadge` isolated with a stub observable
3. **Rung 3** — `CartView` with a real `Cart.Server`
4. **Rung 4** — LiveView end-to-end integration via `Filament.Test.LiveView`

Plus one cross-cutting projection validation: proves that `CartBadge` does NOT
receive a re-render notification when the cart state changes in a way that leaves
the item count unchanged.

This is the most comprehensive H ticket. The all-four-rungs demonstration is what the
plan calls "the rung-3 canonical example."

## Deviation policy

Any deviation from this spec requires prior approval. Stop work, run
`bw comment <ticket-id> "..."` describing the conflict, reopen the ticket, and await
guidance. Do not improvise.

---

## 0. Prerequisites — read implementations first

Before writing any test code, read:

  - `examples/cart/lib/cart/state.ex` — Cart.State struct and add_item/remove_item/item_count
  - `examples/cart/lib/cart/server.ex` — Cart.Server public API (add_item/2, remove_item/2)
  - `examples/cart/lib/cart_web/components/cart_badge.ex` — CartBadge props, projection fn
  - `examples/cart/lib/cart_web/components/cart_view.ex` — CartView props, event closures
  - Wherever F1 placed Filament.Test — check test/support/ or lib/filament/test.ex
    for exact signatures: mount/3, click/2, render_text/1, update/1, eventually/2
  - Wherever F3 placed Filament.Test.LiveView — check the rung-4 wrapper module

The CartBadge uses a projection that extracts only the item count:
  `fn state -> Cart.State.item_count(state) end`
CartView uses the full state (identity projection or no projection).

Confirm exact prop names and component module names from the G2 implementation.

---

## 1. Test file location

FILE: `test/filament/examples/cart_test.exs`

`examples/cart/lib/` is already in `elixirc_paths(:test)` from G2.
All of `Cart.*` and `CartWeb.Components.*` are available.

---

## 2. Rung-1 tests — Cart.State domain (pure, no processes)

```elixir
defmodule Filament.Examples.CartTest do
  use ExUnit.Case, async: true
  import Filament.Test

  # ── Rung 1: Cart.State pure domain ──────────────────────────────────────────

  describe "Cart.State" do
    test "starts empty" do
      state = %Cart.State{}
      assert state.items == []
      assert state.total_cents == 0
      assert Cart.State.item_count(state) == 0
    end

    test "add_item/2 appends and updates total" do
      state = %Cart.State{}
      item = %Cart.Item{id: "a", name: "Widget", price_cents: 999, quantity: 1}
      state2 = Cart.State.add_item(state, item)
      assert Cart.State.item_count(state2) == 1
      assert state2.total_cents == 999
    end

    test "add_item/2 increments quantity for duplicate id" do
      state = %Cart.State{}
      item = %Cart.Item{id: "a", name: "Widget", price_cents: 500, quantity: 1}
      state2 = Cart.State.add_item(state, item)
      state3 = Cart.State.add_item(state2, item)
      assert Cart.State.item_count(state3) == 2
      assert state3.total_cents == 1000
      assert length(state3.items) == 1  # still one distinct item
    end

    test "remove_item/2 removes item and adjusts total" do
      state = %Cart.State{}
      item = %Cart.Item{id: "b", name: "Gadget", price_cents: 2000, quantity: 1}
      state2 = Cart.State.add_item(state, item)
      state3 = Cart.State.remove_item(state2, "b")
      assert state3.items == []
      assert state3.total_cents == 0
    end

    test "remove_item/2 on nonexistent id is a no-op" do
      state = %Cart.State{}
      assert Cart.State.remove_item(state, "nonexistent") == state
    end

    test "item_count/1 sums quantities" do
      state = %Cart.State{
        items: [
          %Cart.Item{id: "a", name: "X", price_cents: 10, quantity: 3},
          %Cart.Item{id: "b", name: "Y", price_cents: 20, quantity: 2}
        ]
      }
      assert Cart.State.item_count(state) == 5
    end
  end
```

## 3. Rung-2 tests — CartBadge with stub observable

CartBadge subscribes to a `Cart.Server` with a projection that returns only the
item count. In Rung 2, replace the real server with a `Filament.Test.Stub`.

The stub's initial function receives a subscription request and returns the
initial value for the subscriber's projection. For CartBadge, the component
passes the projection to `use_observable/3`. The stub initial function should
return the same type the projection would return — i.e., an integer (item count).

Read CartBadge's source to confirm:
- The exact prop name for the server (likely `:server`)
- Whether the projection is defined inside the component or passed as a prop
- What the component renders for count=0 vs count=N

```elixir
  # ── Rung 2: CartBadge isolated (stub observable) ────────────────────────────

  describe "CartBadge (rung-2)" do
    test "renders item count from stub observable" do
      # Stub returns initial count of 0.
      # CartBadge subscribes with a count projection. The stub's fn receives the
      # subscription request (nil or whatever CartBadge passes) and returns the
      # initial projected value. Since CartBadge applies a projection internally,
      # the stub should return the raw Cart.State so the projection can be applied,
      # OR the stub should return the already-projected integer directly.
      #
      # Check CartBadge's use_observable call to determine which.
      # If use_observable(server, nil, project: fn s -> item_count(s) end) is used,
      # then the stub receives the raw state and the projection is applied by
      # Filament.Hooks. Set the stub's fn to return a full %Cart.State{}.
      # If CartBadge calls use_observable(server) with no projection and the server
      # stores and returns the count directly, stub returns an integer.
      #
      # Adapt the stub fn below after reading the implementation:
      {:ok, stub} = Filament.Test.Stub.start(fn _req -> %Cart.State{} end)

      {:ok, view} = mount(CartWeb.Components.CartBadge, %{server: stub},
                          stub: [{CartWeb.Components.CartBadge, fn _req -> %Cart.State{} end}])
      # ^ Adapt: if CartBadge uses a :server prop, you may need to pass the stub pid
      #   directly as the prop rather than using the stub: option in mount/3.
      #   The stub: option registers a stub keyed by server identity (module name or atom).
      #   Pass stub pid as prop if the component uses use_observable(@server, ...).

      text = render_text(view)
      assert text =~ "0"  # adapt to actual rendered text (could be "0 items", "Cart (0)", etc.)
    end

    test "badge updates when count changes" do
      {:ok, stub} = Filament.Test.Stub.start(fn _req -> %Cart.State{} end)
      {:ok, view} = mount(CartWeb.Components.CartBadge, %{server: stub})
      assert render_text(view) =~ "0"

      # Push a new state with one item. CartBadge's projection will extract count=1.
      new_state = Cart.State.add_item(%Cart.State{},
        %Cart.Item{id: "x", name: "Test", price_cents: 100, quantity: 1})
      Filament.Test.Stub.push(stub, new_state)

      # flush_messages processes the {:filament_observable_update, ...} message
      view = Filament.Test.update(view)
      assert render_text(view) =~ "1"
    end

    test "projection: badge does NOT receive update when count is unchanged" do
      # This is the core projection validation from the plan.
      # Scenario: register a manual subscriber with the count projection.
      # Push a state change that does not change the count (same items, different
      # price or metadata). Because item_count is unchanged, change-or-bust should
      # suppress the notification.
      #
      # Since Cart.State.add_item always increments count, simulate "no count change"
      # by pushing the same state twice. The second push should NOT deliver a message
      # because the projected value (count) did not change.
      {:ok, stub} = Filament.Test.Stub.start(fn _req -> %Cart.State{} end)

      # Subscribe manually as a proxy so we can assert/refute receive
      sub = %Filament.Observable.Subscriber{
        pid: self(),
        fiber_id: :badge_test_fiber,
        slot_index: 0,
        project: fn state -> Cart.State.item_count(state) end
      }
      {:ok, _initial} = Filament.Observable.subscribe(stub, nil, sub)

      # First push: count 0 → 1
      state1 = Cart.State.add_item(%Cart.State{},
        %Cart.Item{id: "a", name: "A", price_cents: 100, quantity: 1})
      Filament.Test.Stub.push(stub, state1)
      assert_receive {:filament_observable_update, :badge_test_fiber, 0, 1}, 500

      # Second push: same items, but no count change.
      # Pushing state1 again — count stays at 1 — no notification expected.
      Filament.Test.Stub.push(stub, state1)
      refute_receive {:filament_observable_update, :badge_test_fiber, 0, _}, 100
    end
  end
```

## 4. Rung-3 tests — CartView with real Cart.Server

CartView renders the full cart (item list, total, remove buttons). It uses a real
`Cart.Server` started in the test. After a mutation, call `Filament.Test.update/1`
to drain the `{:filament_observable_update, ...}` message and re-render.

Read `examples/cart/lib/cart_web/components/cart_view.ex` to determine:
- What props CartView accepts (`:server`)
- What it renders for an empty cart vs items
- How "remove" is implemented (likely phx-click that calls Cart.Server.remove_item)
- What the total display looks like (cents as "$N.NN" or raw integer)

```elixir
  # ── Rung 3: CartView with real Cart.Server ──────────────────────────────────

  describe "CartView (rung-3, real Cart.Server)" do
    setup do
      {:ok, server} = Cart.Server.start_link([])
      {:ok, view} = mount(CartWeb.Components.CartView, %{server: server})
      %{server: server, view: view}
    end

    test "renders empty cart", %{view: view} do
      # Adapt text to match actual empty-cart rendering
      text = render_text(view)
      assert text =~ "empty" or text =~ "0" or text == ""
    end

    test "add_item updates rendered view", %{server: server, view: view} do
      Cart.Server.add_item(server, %Cart.Item{
        id: "w1", name: "Widget", price_cents: 999, quantity: 1
      })
      view = Filament.Test.update(view)
      assert render_text(view) =~ "Widget"
    end

    test "remove_item via click updates rendered view", %{server: server, view: view} do
      Cart.Server.add_item(server, %Cart.Item{
        id: "g1", name: "Gadget", price_cents: 500, quantity: 1
      })
      view = Filament.Test.update(view)
      assert render_text(view) =~ "Gadget"

      # Click the remove button. Adapt selector to match actual rendered HTML.
      {:ok, view} = click(view, "[phx-click][data-item-id='g1']")
      # After the click, the event closure calls Cart.Server.remove_item/2,
      # which notifies observers. flush_messages processes the update.
      assert render_text(view) =~ "" # "Gadget" no longer present
      refute render_text(view) =~ "Gadget"
    end

    test "eventually/2 retries until cart is updated asynchronously", %{server: server, view: view} do
      # Spawn an asynchronous mutation and use eventually/2 to wait for it.
      spawn(fn ->
        Process.sleep(50)
        Cart.Server.add_item(server, %Cart.Item{
          id: "async1", name: "AsyncItem", price_cents: 100, quantity: 1
        })
      end)

      # view is captured by the closure; update it inside eventually
      view_ref = :erlang.make_ref()
      Process.put(view_ref, view)

      Filament.Test.eventually(fn ->
        current = Process.get(view_ref)
        updated = Filament.Test.update(current)
        Process.put(view_ref, updated)
        render_text(updated) =~ "AsyncItem"
      end, timeout: 500)
    end
  end
```

NOTE: The `eventually/2` pattern above uses Process dictionary to mutate the captured
view reference across retries. This is a known pattern for eventually-based tests in
Filament. If `Filament.Test.eventually/2` has a different signature or expects a
different interaction model, adapt to match what F2 actually built.

---

## 5. Rung-4 test — LiveView integration

Use `Filament.Test.LiveView` (built in F3) to test the Cart page via a real LiveView
connection. F3 wraps `Phoenix.LiveViewTest`.

Read `Filament.Test.LiveView` (from Track F, ticket flm-j92.4) to see its exact API.
The host LiveView for the cart example is in `examples/cart/lib/cart_web/live/cart_live.ex`.

Check whether the cart example has a LiveView module and an Endpoint configured.
If there is no `CartWeb.Endpoint` or the example is not set up as a full Phoenix app
for test purposes, confirm with a comment on this ticket before proceeding.

Rung-4 tests are inherently more fragile and slow. Include one "smoke test" that mounts
the LiveView and confirms the basic cart page renders without errors.

```elixir
  # ── Rung 4: LiveView integration ────────────────────────────────────────────

  # NOTE: Rung-4 requires CartWeb.Endpoint to be started in test config.
  # If this is not set up in the cart example, skip this describe block and
  # comment on the ticket explaining the gap.

  describe "CartLive (rung-4)" do
    @tag :rung4
    test "mounts the cart LiveView and renders initial state" do
      # Adapt to the actual Filament.Test.LiveView API from F3.
      # The rung-4 wrapper should look similar to Phoenix.LiveViewTest.live/2.
      {:ok, view, _html} = Filament.Test.LiveView.live(build_conn(), "/cart")
      assert render(view) =~ "Cart"
    end
  end
```

If Rung 4 is not feasible (endpoint not configured, etc.), replace with a comment block
explaining why and open a sub-ticket if work is needed to make it feasible.

---

## 6. Run tests

```
# Run just H2
mix test test/filament/examples/cart_test.exs

# Run all examples tests
mix test test/filament/examples/
```

- [ ] Rung-4: LiveView smoke test passes, OR blocked with a comment + sub-ticket created
